entries.title: Dinah and the events at Shechem
Moses' birth and rescue from the Nile
Individual confrontations during the ten plagues
entries.editorialNote: Five Exodus chapters contain multiple separate confrontations; read chapter by chapter and do not conflate individual plagues into one episode.

entries.title: The golden calf and Moses' intercession
Construction and consecration of the Tabernacle
entries.editorialNote: Exodus 35–40 includes detailed fabrication, appointment and erection of the Tabernacle; do not advertise every verse as a compact episode.

entries.title: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses
Achan's sin and the defeat at Ai
Capture and return of the Ark
Saul and the woman of Endor
Elijah and the widow of Sarepta
Elijah confronts the prophets of Baal
Elijah is taken up to heaven
Isaiah's call and vision of God's holiness
Josiah discovers the Book of the Law
Daniel and his companions at Babylon's court
The three young men in the fiery furnace
Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall
Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem's walls
entries.editorialNote: Nehemiah 2–6 spans multiple events and participants, not one dramatic scene.

entries.title: Martyrdom of the seven brothers and their mother
Judas Maccabeus purifies and rededicates the Temple
Prayer and sacrifice for the dead
The Visitation
entries.editorialNote: Visitation Luke 1:39–56 contains the Magnificat also indexed separately. Both point to the same witness verse records.

entries.title: Birth of St John the Baptist
Presentation of Jesus in the Temple
Twelve-year-old Jesus among the doctors in the Temple
entries.editorialNote: Luke 2:41–52 includes the Finding in the Temple and return to Nazareth; distinguish from the hidden-life index.

entries.title: Forty days and temptations in the wilderness
Simon of Cyrene and the women of Jerusalem
Angel's announcement to the women
entries.editorialNote: Keep Matthew's women-at-tomb testimony distinct from other Gospel accounts.

entries.title: Appearance beside the Sea of Galilee
entries.editorialNote: John 21:1–14 includes the miraculous catch already separately indexed in John 21:4–11.

entries.title: Jesus asks Peter three times whether he loves Him
Martyrdom of James, brother of John
entries.editorialNote: Acts 12:1–2 is contained within Peter's imprisonment narrative index Acts 12:1–19. Do not present it as the same event.

entries.title: Paul heals a man at Lystra
Paul and Silas are imprisoned at Philippi
Paul addresses the Areopagus at Athens
Paul's farewell to the elders at Miletus
John sees the risen Christ on Patmos
entries.editorialNote: Patmos revelation is introduced with a historical visionary witness, not a date-ordered future chronicle.

entries.title: Messages to the seven churches
entries.editorialNote: These are prophetic addresses within Revelation, not seven autonomous historical plots.

entries.title: The heavenly throne and twenty-four elders
Opening of the seven seals
entries.editorialNote: The seventh seal opens at Revelation 8:1; verse 8:6 initiates the trumpet sequence. Preserve the boundary rather than presenting trumpet descriptions as part of the seals.

entries.title: The seven trumpets
entries.editorialNote: The trumpet sequence starts at Revelation 8:6; Revelation 8:1–5 belongs to the seventh seal. Chapters 9–11 contain interludes and later trumpet material; no claim of uniform action on every verse.

entries.title: The woman clothed with the sun and the dragon
entries.editorialNote: The woman, sun and dragon are visionary images; do not turn a patristic reading into a literal contemporary event.

entries.title: The beast from the sea
entries.editorialNote: The beast coming from the sea is described in 13:1–10; chapter 13:11 begins the distinct beast from the earth. These are two reading views over one chapter, not two versions of the Scripture text.

entries.title: The beast from the earth
entries.editorialNote: The beast from the earth first appears at Revelation 13:11, not 13:1. Keep its source verses separate from the sea beast.

entries.title: The seven last plagues
entries.editorialNote: The last plagues are visionary scenes, not a dated earthly itinerary.

entries.title: The fall of Babylon
entries.editorialNote: Babylon's fall in Revelation is an apocalyptic image and must not automatically become a historical dated city event.
